newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND HELD TO DRAW BY HERTHA BERLIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND HELD TO DRAW BY HERTHA BERLIN.

text.p: European Cup holders Borussia Dortmund were held to a 1-1 draw in front of a capacity 76,000 crowd at Hertha Berlin in their first game of the German league season on Sunday.
Lars Ricken put Dortmund into the lead in the 26th minute with a harmless-looking shot from outside the penalty area that nonetheless found the back of the net after a cruel deflection.
Newly-promoted Hertha's equaliser seven minutes later owed something to luck as well. An effort by striker Antek Covic hit team mate Sixten Veit before creeping past Dortmund goalkeeper Stefan Klos.

Hamburg were saved from a home defeat by Borussia Moenchengladbach with a 90th-minute headed goal from Bosnian Hasan Salihamidzic that put them level at 2-2. Swedish striker Joergen Pettersson scored both the Moenchengladbach goals.
With all opening games of the season now played, Karlsruhe have taken an early lead in the German first division after their 3-1 defeat of Werder Bremen on Saturday.
Champions Bayern Munich are languishing in joint 15th place after their shock 1-0 defeat to Kaiserlautern.
